Willful

WILL-ful -- first syllable just like the word 'will'. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Willful is intentional or deliberate, often in a stubborn or defiant way.

The report blamed the spill on the company's willful disregard of three separate safety warnings.

Worked Example

Even after three warnings from the referee, the player keeps shoving opponents, fully aware of the rule he is breaking each time.

Breaking the rules on purpose, knowing exactly what he is doing, is what makes the behavior willful. Unlike 'accidental,' which means unintended, willful means done deliberately -- and it usually carries a stubborn, defiant edge.

How Willful Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

deliberate

deliberate: done consciously and on purpose

headstrong

headstrong: determined to have one's own way

obstinate

obstinate: stubbornly refusing to change one's course

Antonyms

accidental

accidental: happening by chance, not on purpose

obedient

obedient: willing to follow rules or instructions

How Strong Is It? — deliberate → obstinate → willful

deliberate vs. willful

deliberate vs. willful: Deliberate is more neutral than willful -- a deliberate act is simply done on purpose, while a willful act adds a layer of stubborn defiance, as if the person knew better and did it anyway.

obstinate vs. willful

obstinate vs. willful: Obstinate can feel even more stubborn than willful: willful stresses that an act was intentional and defiant, while obstinate describes someone who digs in and refuses to budge no matter what anyone says.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — will

root — will: desire, intention (Old English willa)

suffix — -ful

suffix — -ful: full of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Willful is simply will ('desire, intention') plus -ful ('full of'). Someone willful is so full of their own will that they push ahead with their intentions no matter the rules or warnings.

Use the root in a new word: hopeful

Use the root in a new word: hopeful: The young actor stayed hopeful even after a dozen auditions ended in rejection.

Root Check

Word Choice

Willful almost always carries a disapproving edge. Phrases like 'willful disobedience,' 'willful ignorance,' and 'willful neglect' all suggest someone who knew better and stubbornly did the wrong thing anyway -- it is stronger and more negative than simply 'purposeful.'
